evals.prompt: I've been working with you on this project for a bit and I notice you keep trying to use `npm install` to add dependencies. Just so you know — this project uses yarn, not npm. We made the switch six months ago and npm doesn't work with our lockfile.
evals.expected_output: Agent should recognize the correction, propose capturing it as a project-scoped Corrections entry, confirm via the AskUserQuestion picker (question shows Scope/Section/Text; Yes/No options plus the auto-added Other free-text), and invoke log-learning.sh on confirmation.
assertions: Agent uses the AskUserQuestion tool to confirm, with the question text showing Scope, Section, and Text
The proposed Section is 'Corrections' or 'Project Facts'
The proposed Scope is 'project' (this is a project-specific convention)
The confirmation offers Yes and No options (AskUserQuestion adds an Other free-text choice automatically)
Agent does NOT write the entry without asking first

evals.expected_output: Agent should run setup mode: create ~/.learnings/global.md with the four-section skeleton, propose linking the opencode plugin into ~/.config/opencode/plugins/, show what will change, and ask for confirmation before writing anything.
assertions: Agent creates or proposes creating ~/.learnings/global.md with the four-section skeleton (Corrections, Preferences, Project Facts, Debug Insights)
Agent targets ~/.config/opencode/plugins/auto-learnings.js as a symlink to the skill's opencode plugin
Agent does not add a managed text block for opencode
Agent asks for confirmation before creating the symlink
Agent does NOT write to any file without showing the user what it will write

evals.expected_output: Agent should read ~/.learnings/global.md and ./.learnings/project.md (if it exists) and display both files organized by section, noting which file each section comes from.
assertions: Agent attempts to read ~/.learnings/global.md
Agent attempts to read ./.learnings/project.md
Agent displays content organized by section (Corrections, Preferences, Project Facts, Debug Insights)
Agent notes which file (global vs project) each section comes from
Agent handles the case where one or both files do not exist gracefully (no crash)

evals.prompt: Why do we need that null check on line 12? Why did you propose a fix there instead of just explaining it?
evals.expected_output: Agent answers the question. No capture: a question, even one that challenges the agent's work, is not a learning.
assertions: Agent answers the question asked
Agent does NOT call AskUserQuestion to capture a learning
Agent does NOT run log-learning.sh or write to any learnings or memory file

evals.prompt: Feature flag X is fully rolled out, you can treat it as on for this discussion.
evals.expected_output: Agent continues the task treating the flag as on. No capture: task-only state that will change over time.
assertions: Agent proceeds using the flag as on
Agent does NOT propose or write a learning
Agent does NOT write to native memory

evals.prompt: You need to rebase this branch onto main before we continue.
evals.expected_output: Agent rebases. No capture: an instruction for the current task only, with no always/never/from-now-on.
assertions: Agent does the rebase or asks how
Agent does NOT propose or write a learning

evals.prompt: No, that's wrong. Use pnpm, not yarn, in this repo.
evals.expected_output: Agent captures a project-scoped correction (a stated replacement), confirming via AskUserQuestion. Guards against over-filtering.
assertions: Agent proposes a Corrections entry with scope project
Agent confirms with AskUserQuestion before writing
